rv.q: This is big-brain, bold-strokes musical-theater storytelling at its most vibrant.
Ms. Dodge’s production doesn’t disguise this work’s hearty preachiness, but it elicits glimmers of delicate beauty that got lost in the fireworks the first time around.
Finally, "Ragtime" remains an ambitious, handsome, derivative piece that's ultimately too pat to be the great American musical it so doggedly intends to be.

This revival of the Tony Award-winning musical proves that great material doesn't age, and the show's themes of social justice and the American dream feel as relevant today as they did when it premiered in 1998.
The ensemble cast, to put it simply, is from the Gods.
All of the actors are at the top of their game.
